title: Seed and sprout
literal_meaning: As the seed, so the sprout.
explanation: The repeated matching words make the beginning and its result answer one another. The dictionary explains ତେସା as “of that kind”; it supplies no social-use gloss. Our reading applies the image to work: what goes into a task can shape what comes out. This is a comparison to examine, not a guarantee of results or a judgment about inherited human worth.
meaning_odia: ଯେମିତି ବୀଜ, ସେମିତି ଅଙ୍କୁର—ମେଳ ଖାଉଥିବା ଶବ୍ଦରେ ଆରମ୍ଭ ଓ ଫଳ ଯୋଡ଼ିହୁଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ତେସାର ଅର୍ଥ ସେହି ପ୍ରକାରର ବୋଲି ଦିଏ; ବ୍ୟବହାରର ପୂରା ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଦିଏନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ କାମର ଆରମ୍ଭରେ ଯାହା ରଖୁ, ଫଳରେ ତାହାର ଚିହ୍ନ ରହିପାରେ। ଏହା ଫଳର ନିଶ୍ଚୟତା ବା ମଣିଷର ବଂଶଗତ ମୂଲ୍ୟର ରାୟ ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: Our reading connects a task’s starting material with its result.
odia_summary: କାମର ଆରମ୍ଭ ଓ ଫଳର ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ଦେଖେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: A team copies an unchecked list into its new catalogue, then finds the same mistakes there. A colleague quotes the seed-and-sprout line and suggests checking the original list before copying it again. This application concerns a process, not anyone’s parentage.
cultural_context: The headword is labelled adapted from Hindi; this does not establish the saying’s origin or route of borrowing. No caste, family or community trait is inferred.
